questions.label: Questions
questions.description: JSON map of question id to a typed question. Answers come back under the same ids as data.answers.<id>.

state.label: State
state.description: What to decide about: a ticket, a record, a message. Text is sent as text; JSON is sent as structured state.

response.description: { model, answers, usage }. answers is keyed by the question ids you sent, never by position, and every answer is a typed value, not text. A choice answer is { type: 'choice', choice: string (the winning option key), probabilities: record<option, number>, confidence: number 0-1 }. A noul (yes/no) answer is { type: 'noul', noul: number } where noul is the probability of yes from 0 to 1 and there is no separate confidence. A score answer is { type: 'score', score: number (probability-weighted position from 0 to levels-1), legend: record<index, level text>, probabilities: record<index, number>, confidence: number }. Bind queries.<q>.data.answers.<id>.choice, .noul or .score; show a score's level with data.answers.<id>.legend[Math.round(data.answers.<id>.score)]. usage carries input_tokens, output_tokens and cost.

notes: questions is a JSON map of question id to a typed question { type: 'choice' | 'noul' | 'score', instructions, criteria }. choice needs criteria as a map of at least two option keys to descriptions; score needs criteria as an ordered list of at least two levels written as concrete situations; noul takes instructions only. Question ids are for your bindings and are not sent to the model, so put the full meaning in instructions.

state is what the questions are about: pass a record or an object of named fields such as {{ { subject: components.table1.selectedRow.subject, body: components.table1.selectedRow.body } }} rather than whole rows or pages; the model reads literally and unrelated detail lowers accuracy. A plain string is sent as text.

Ask every independent question about the same state in one query: they run in parallel and one call costs a few hundred milliseconds. Use a second query only when an answer decides what state to fetch next.

Decide thresholds in code or bindings, not in the question: a noul of 0.5 means yes and no are equally likely, not a medium intensity, and a spread choice distribution means several options were acceptable.
model is optional. Blank uses jev-latest on a TypeSafe credential and typesafe/jev-1.13 on an OpenRouter credential; a bare name such as jev-1.13 is mapped to the right form for either credential.
The plugin validates question shapes before calling the API, so a malformed question fails with a message naming the question id; a 401 means the key for the selected credential mode is wrong.
